log.action: Draw my sword and rush toward the South Road.
log.narration: Turn 1 | Day 1, 6:00 pmPerception checkd20: 17 -- successYou wrench the longsword free, ash falling from the scabbard's mouth like a dying breath, and break into a run. Boots pound the hard-packed earth as the dust cloud swells ahead, resolving into shapes: a wagon canted hard on a broken wheel, oxen bellowing and thrashing in their traces, bodies already down in the road. Raiders in mismatched leather and stolen mail move among the wreckage with the unhurried cruelty of men who have done this many times before, cutting down anyone too slow or too brave. One of them, a rangy figure with a notched axe and a voice like gravel dragged over stone, barks orders at the others, and something in the set of his shoulders claws up out of your memory like a hook dragging up a drowned thing.You are close enough now to see the brand on that man's forearm, a twisted sigil scorched into old scar tissue, and your gut goes cold before your mind catches up to why.Nolan's head snaps up as you close the last of the distance, and recognition splits his scarred face into something between a grin and a snarl."Well. Look what the ash blew in."🔊………

log.action: Move cautiously toward the dust cloud, staying low.
log.narration: Turn 2 | Day 1, 6:00 pmYou drop into a crouch, but your blood is already up and your feet betray your caution, carrying you fast and low across the broken ground. There is no cover here, only the drifting ash and the wreck of the wagon, and Nolan Grimtide has already marked you. He does not charge. He plants his boots and lifts a hand, calling off the nearer raider still stripping a corpse of its purse, and that one turns from his looting with a rusty falchion already dripping."Hold, hold. Let the big one come to me. I want to see his face when he understands."You are within striking distance now, close enough to smell the raider's sweat and the copper reek of the dead. Nolan's raiders spread wide, boxing the wagon, and the one nearest you grins with broken teeth, falchion low and ready to gut you the moment you close.🔊………

log.action: Attack the nearest Slaver Raider before he strikes.
log.narration: Turn 3 | Day 1, 6:00 pmStrength check (attack roll)d20: 19 -- successYou commit to the strike, blade angling for the gap between the raider's ribs before his own swing can gather weight.Power Strike declared. Your longsword takes him just under the arm, biting through leather and meat in one brutal draw, and he folds around the wound with a strangled grunt, the falchion falling from fingers that no longer answer him.He is dead before he hits the ash, and the second raider flanking the wagon jerks back a step, eyes wide at how fast his companion went down. Nolan Grimtide does not flinch. He watches you over the wreckage with those flat, amused eyes, working his jaw like a man chewing over an old debt."Still fast. Still stupid enough to charge a superior number. Some men never learn what the collar taught them."The remaining raider grips his blade tighter and begins circling wide, looking to come at your flank while Nolan simply waits, in no hurry at all, letting the moment stretch like a man savoring a good meal before he eats it.🔊………

log.action: Shove past the raider to reach Nolan directly.
log.narration: Turn 4 | Day 1, 6:00 pmStrength check (shove)d20: 16 -- successDexterity saving throwd20: 13 -- successYou do not wait for the flanking raider to find his angle. You drive your shoulder into him as you pass, using your weight like a battering ram, and he goes stumbling sideways into the shattered wagon wheel with a curse.He crashes hard against the splintered wood and goes down tangled in the spokes, cursing and scrabbling for purchase, bought you the opening you needed. Nolan's grin does not waver as you close on him. He rolls his shoulders, unhooks the notched axe from his belt in one smooth motion, and settles into a stance that speaks of old brutal training, the kind beaten into a man in a pit, not taught in any yard."There he is. Come on then, dog. Let's see if the collar's memory still bites."He does not wait for you to set your feet. He swings first, the axe whistling in a low arc meant to open your gut, and only your instincts, honed in places just as brutal as wherever forged him, snap your body back half a step.The axe head hisses past a hand's width from your belly, close enough that you feel the wind of it, and Nolan snarls in frustration as his momentum carries him half a turn off balance.🔊………

log.action: Retreat toward the wagon to guard my flank.
log.narration: Turn 5 | Day 1, 6:00 pmPerception checkd20: 15 -- successYou back off two hard steps, boots skidding in the ash, until the shattered wagon bed is at your shoulder and nothing can come at you from behind but splintered wood. Nolan recovers his balance and stalks after you, unhurried, axe held low and loose the way a man holds a tool he trusts completely."Running already? Valerius said you'd have more spine left in you than this."The name lands in your chest like a dropped stone, cold and sudden, dragging up images you have spent years trying to drown in ale and distance. The downed raider claws himself free of the wagon wheel behind Nolan, blade recovered, murder in his eyes, and moves to circle wide toward your unguarded side even as Nolan closes the last of the gap between you.You catch the raider's boot scuff against loose gravel an instant before he'd have been on you, giving you just enough warning to angle your shoulder and keep both men in your sight rather than let one slip behind your guard.🔊………

log.action: Shout a challenge, demanding he name his master.
log.narration: Turn 6 | Day 1, 6:00 pmDexterity saving throwd20: 9 -- failedYou plant your feet against the wagon bed and roar the demand across the ash-choked ground, blade leveled at his chest."Say it! Say the name, Grimtide! Whose leash are you on now?"Nolan barks a laugh, harsh and delighted, axe still weaving that slow patient arc as he closes the distance."You already heard it, dog. Valerius sends his regards, and an invitation. Join him again, or bleed out here with the rest of these cattle."He does not wait for your answer. He lunges in with the axe, aiming to hook your sword arm and drag you off balance, but the flanking raider chooses that same instant to rush your unguarded side, blade thrusting for your ribs.The raider's blade scrapes along your ribs under the chainmail's edge, a hot line of pain, but Nolan's axe hook goes wide as you twist away from the worse of it, iron links grinding but holding.🔊………

log.action: Snatch up the fallen falchion to arm off-hand.
log.narration: Turn 7 | Day 1, 6:00 pmDexterity checkd20: 14 -- successYou drop into a crouch and your free hand closes on the notched falchion the first raider dropped when your blade found his ribs, ash-dusted and still slick with his blood. You come up with steel in both fists, longsword in your right, stolen falchion in your left, and Nolan's grin falters just a fraction at the sight of it.The weight is wrong in your off hand, unfamiliar balance, but your instincts do not care what shape the steel takes, only that it cuts."Two blades won't save you from what's coming, Korrag. Valerius doesn't send for men he means to let walk away twice."The raider beside him surges in first, thrusting low for your gut while Nolan circles to pin you between them, and you have half a heartbeat to answer both or die between them.🔊………

log.action: Use Shield Wall to brace against both attackers.
log.narration: Turn 8 | Day 1, 6:00 pmConstitution saving throwd20: 17 -- successYou plant your boots and drop your weight low, angling your body so the wagon's broken side timbers guard your back, bracing like a man behind a wall of iron that isn't there.Shield Wall raised. The raider's low thrust catches your hip instead of your gut, the blow skidding off muscle gone tense as rope, and Nolan's follow-up hook glances off your forearm guard with a jarring clang that numbs your fingers but draws no blood.Both strikes land soft where they should have landed hard, your braced stance eating the worst of the force, and you feel the ache settle into your bones rather than open in your flesh. Nolan curses and steps back half a pace, reassessing, while the raider beside him grits his teeth and readies another thrust, unwilling to break off now that blood is close.🔊………

log.action: Cut down the flanking raider before he closes.
log.narration: Turn 9 | Day 1, 6:00 pmStrength check (attack)d20: 18 -- successYou do not wait for his blade to find you a second time. You pivot on your back foot and bring the stolen falchion around in a short brutal arc, catching his overextended thrust and driving the point up under his guard while your longsword follows through with the killing stroke.Power Strike declared.The longsword opens his throat in a single vicious draw, and he drops without another sound, choking on the ash and his own blood as he crumples across his dead companion. Nolan does not so much as glance at the corpse. His flat eyes stay locked on you, jaw working, and something like respect flickers there beneath the old savage hunger."Always were fast. Faster than fair, some said."He shifts his grip on the axe, circling now that it is only the two of you left standing among the wreckage and the dead.🔊………

log.action: Slam Nolan with the wagon's broken timber.
log.narration: Turn 10 | Day 1, 6:00 pmStrength check (improvised weapon)d20: 17 -- successYou grab a length of splintered timber jutting from the wagon's broken frame and wrench it free, then swing it in a wide crushing arc before Nolan can bring his axe to bear. It catches him full across the shoulder and ribs, the wood cracking with the force of the blow, and he staggers sideways with a grunt of pain, axe arm dropping for one crucial heartbeat.Weapon Mastery holds true even with rough timber in your grip, no clumsiness in the strike, only weight and fury finding their mark. Nolan reels back against the wagon's ruined side, blood welling at his mouth, and for the first time his grin slips entirely into something raw and afraid."Wait... wait, damn you. I yield. I yield!"He drops the axe in the ash, both hands raised, chest heaving, the old savage light in his eyes finally gone dark with fear of dying here in the ruin he helped make.🔊………

log.action: Demand Nolan tell me where Valerius can be found.
log.narration: Turn 11 | Day 1, 6:00 pmYou stand over him with the timber still in your fist, splinters dark with his blood, and press the point of your longsword to the hollow of his throat instead of finishing it. He goes very still, breath ragged, hands trembling where he holds them raised."Where. Where do I find him."Nolan swallows hard against the blade's edge, eyes darting to the dead scattered around you both, and something in him breaks, the old bravado gone out like a snuffed torch."Ashenveil. The High Gate, then deeper, the fighting pits under the old temple district. He's not just running slaves anymore, Korrag. He's a priest now. High priest of something that doesn't have a kind name. The brand, the one on my arm, it isn't just a mark of ownership anymore. It's a mouth. It's how he listens to the Reach."He laughs, cracked and half mad, blood flecking his lips."You should've stayed dead to him. He doesn't forget his wolves."🔊………

log.action: Press the timber to his throat and press for truth.
log.narration: Turn 12 | Day 1, 6:00 pmYou lean the timber's splintered edge harder against him, but there is no more truth left to press from him, only silence and the ash settling over what is already done. Nolan Grimtide lies where your first strike put him, and the words you thought you heard were only the wind combing through the wreckage and your own blood roaring in your ears. Whatever answer you sought, you will not find it in a dead man's mouth twice.You straighten slowly, chest heaving, the crossroads gone quiet but for the creak of the ruined wagon and the distant caw of carrion birds already circling overhead, drawn to the stink of blood and torn earth.The road south waits, ash-pale and empty, leading toward Ashenveil and whatever Valerius has built beneath it. The name still burns where Nolan first spoke it, a debt owed and long overdue.🔊………

log.action: Bind Nolan's wounds despite everything he's confessed.
log.narration: Turn 13 | Day 1, 6:00 pmYou drop to a knee beside him anyway, some old instinct or stubborn guilt driving your hands toward the wound, but the flesh under your palms is already cold, already still. There is no wound left to bind, only the ruin your timber and steel made of a man you once called brother-in-arms. The ash has begun to settle into the creases of his face, patient as snow, and no amount of pressure or will brings breath back into a chest that stopped fighting for it turns ago.You kneel there a moment longer than you mean to, jaw tight, the wind dragging grit across both of you."Should've stayed dead to me too, Nolan."The words come out rough, half curse and half apology, and then you rise, wiping your hands on your thighs though there is nothing there to wipe away but old blood long dried. The crossroads holds its silence. Somewhere south the High Gate of Ashenveil waits, and beyond it, buried under some rotten temple, the man who made a brand into a mouth and a mouth into a leash.🔊………

log.action: Search the dead raiders for coin or clues.
log.narration: Turn 14 | Day 1, 6:00 pmInvestigation checkd20: 16 -- successYou move among the fallen with the flat, practiced efficiency of a man who has looted corpses before and felt nothing much doing it. The first raider yields little, a few scarred coins and a whetstone worn thin as paper. The second carries a stained leather satchel, and inside it your fingers close on a folded scrap of parchment, sealed once in black wax now cracked and flaking away like dead skin.You unfold it carefully. The hand that wrote it was careful too, elegant even, utterly at odds with the men who carried it. A few lines only, addressed to no one by name, speaking of a shipment to be delivered whole and unmarked to the pits beneath the temple district, and signed with a single sigil burned into the wax itself, a chained crown pressed small and precise. You have seen that mark before, seared into flesh rather than wax. Nolan's arm bore its twin.The rest of the bodies give up nothing but stink and flies already gathering despite the cold. You straighten, letter tucked against your chest, the ash wind picking at its torn edge. The road south is calling louder now, and it has a name written on it in wax and blood both.🔊………

log.action: Search Nolan's body for anything marking his master.
log.narration: Turn 15 | Day 1, 6:00 pmYou crouch over Nolan a last time, turning out the pouch at his belt, running your fingers along the inside of his boot. Nothing more there but a broken tooth of flint and a coin worn smooth from years of thumbing. His forearm is the only true document he ever carried, that brand still dark and puckered even in death, the chained crown burned into meat the same as it was burned into wax. You have your answer now, written twice over, once in ink and once in scar tissue.You rise from the dead man's side and look south, where the road runs pale and long toward the High Gate. Whatever waits beneath Ashenveil's temple district, it has a name and a face now, and both belong to Valerius.🔊………

log.action: Head south down the South Road toward the High Gate.
log.narration: Turn 15 | Day 1, 6:00 pmYou crouch over Nolan a last time, turning out the pouch at his belt, running your fingers along the inside of his boot. Nothing more there but a broken tooth of flint and a coin worn smooth from years of thumbing. His forearm is the only true document he ever carried, that brand still dark and puckered even in death, the chained crown burned into meat the same as it was burned into wax. Whatever waits beneath Ashenveil's temple district, it has a name and a face now, and both belong to Valerius.🔊Take the South Road toward the High Gate.Bury or burn Nolan's body before leaving.Check the wrecked wagon for salvageable supplies.

log.action: Bury or burn Nolan's body before leaving.
log.narration: Turn 16 | Day 1, 6:00 pmThere's no shovel and the ground here is packed hard as stone, so you drag deadwood from the shattered wagon instead, splintered planks and a broken axle, piling them over Nolan's body with a grunt that owes nothing to grief and everything to old debts. You strike flint against steel until a spark catches the driest of the wood, and the fire climbs slow and then sudden, hungry, curling black smoke into the ash-gray sky.You stand back and watch it burn, arms crossed, saying nothing, because there is nothing left worth saying to a dead man who chose his master over his own kind. The other bodies you leave to the carrion birds, already dropping low and impatient. When the flames have done their work you turn from the crossroads and do not look back again.South lies Ashenveil, the High Gate rising somewhere beyond the ash haze, and beneath its temple district a debt still waiting to be paid in full.🔊………

log.action: Check the wrecked wagon for salvageable supplies.
log.narration: Turn 17 | Day 1, 6:20 pmYou pick through the wreckage before the fire dies, boots crunching over scattered grain and shattered pottery. Most of the cargo is ruined, flour spilled and soaked black with blood, crates stove in by hooves and axe blows. But beneath a torn canvas you find a coil of good rope, a waterskin still sloshing full, and a small belt pouch that rattles with coin when you shake it loose from a dead man's grip.The oxen are long gone, bolted off into the ash-scrub when the fighting started, and the wagon itself is fit for nothing now but kindling. You sling the rope over one shoulder, sling the letter and coin into your pack, and stand a moment longer in the settling dusk. The road south waits, pale and empty, and somewhere at its end a gate rises over a city that owes you blood.🔊………

log.action: Examine the sealed letter's chained crown sigil closely.
log.narration: Turn 18 | Day 1, 6:20 pmYou crouch by the dying pyre and unfold the letter again, tilting it toward the last gray light. The sigil is pressed deep into what remains of the black wax, a crown wrought in iron links rather than gold, each link rendered so fine you can almost count them. There's a deliberate cruelty in the design, a crown that binds rather than adorns, and beneath it a single word in that same careful hand you remember from before: temple.No other markings, no signature, nothing but that chained crown and the promise of a shipment bound for whatever waits beneath Ashenveil's old temple district. You fold it away again, the parchment stiff with old ash, and rise to your feet. The fire behind you has burned down to embers and bone, and the road south is calling louder now than it was a moment ago.🔊………

log.action: Follow the East trail into the Blighted Reach.
log.narration: Turn 19 | Day 1, 6:50 pmYour ribs burn with every stride, the gash beneath your chainmail still weeping slow and dark, no herb or bandage having touched it since the blade first found you. You press a fold of torn cloak against the wound before it can slow you further, cinching it tight with a grunt, blood already soaking through by the time you've walked a hundred paces. It will need proper tending soon or fester in this ash-choked air, but for now it holds, and you turn your feet from the South Road's promise of Ashenveil to follow the narrower track east instead, the one that winds into the Blighted Reach itself.The land changes fast once you leave the crossroads behind. Ash deepens underfoot like dirty snow, and the wind carries that sweetish rot smell stronger here, thick enough to taste. Skeletal trees claw up from the gray earth, bark blackened and leafless, and somewhere off in the murk you hear a sound that might be wind through dead branches or might be something breathing.Somewhere ahead, faint on the wind, you catch the sound of chains dragging over stone.🔊………

log.action: Draw my longsword and creep toward the chain sound.
log.narration: Turn 20 | Day 1, 6:50 pmStealth checkd20: 16 -- successSteel whispers free of the scabbard, and you fall into a low crouch, boots finding the quieter patches of ash between crackling deadfall. The dragging sound comes again, iron links scraping over broken stone, slow and rhythmic, like something being hauled rather than walking on its own power. You move tree to tree, using the char-black trunks for cover, and the smell of rot thickens with every step until it coats the back of your throat.Through a screen of skeletal branches you find the source. A figure kneels in a hollow of ash, dragging a length of rusted chain across a flat stone slab in long, grinding strokes, over and over, as though sharpening something that was never meant to hold an edge. Its back is to you, hunched and wrong, shoulder blades pressing too sharp against tattered cloth, and when it pauses to tilt its head skyward you see the flesh of its throat has split open in a second, lipless mouth.You've heard men whisper of things like this in the pits, half-truths and drunk men's stories, but you've never stood this close to one before. Whatever it is, it hasn't noticed you yet.🔊………

log.action: Press the makeshift bandage tighter and press onward.
log.narration: Turn 21 | Day 1, 6:50 pmYou cinch the blood-soaked cloth tighter against your ribs, biting down on the flare of pain, and force your breath shallow and silent. The wound answers with a hot throb that runs down into your gut, but it holds, for now. You ease forward another few paces, boots finding bare stone where the ash thins, longsword low and ready at your side.The creature's chain-dragging stops.Its spine cracks as it turns, vertebrae popping wet and wrong beneath the tattered cloth, and the second mouth in its throat gapes wider, tasting the air. Whatever passes for eyes in that ruined face finds you crouched in the dead branches, and a sound claws out of it that is not quite a growl and not quite a word, wet and grinding like the chain against stone.It surges up onto bent, wrong-jointed legs and comes at you fast, far faster than something so broken has any right to move, dragging its iron chain behind it like a tail of rust and teeth.🔊………

log.action: Throw a stone to test its reaction from a distance.
log.narration: Turn 22 | Day 1, 6:50 pmDexterity checkd20: 11 -- failedenemy attack rolld20: 17 -- hitThere's no time for testing. The thing is already closing, chain hissing across stone behind it, and a thrown pebble would do nothing but waste the half-second you have to set your feet. You snatch up a fist-sized rock all the same, some old pit-instinct screaming at you to buy a heartbeat, and hurl it hard into that ruined, gaping throat-mouth.The stone goes wide, cracking off a blackened tree trunk instead, and the Chain-Dragger doesn't so much as flinch. It closes the last of the distance in two lurching strides, chain whipping up and around in a vicious arc aimed at your skull.The links catch you across the temple and shoulder, a burst of white light behind your eyes, and you stagger back against a charred trunk, tasting blood and ash both. The creature looms over you now, wet throat working, rusted chain already coiling back for another strike.🔊………

log.action: Sidestep the chain and slash at its flank.
log.narration: Turn 23 | Day 1, 6:50 pmStrength attack rolld20: 18 -- hitYour head still rings from the last blow, but pit-instinct answers before thought does. You throw your weight sideways as the chain comes whistling around again, and the rusted links crack against bark instead of bone, spraying black splinters. In the same motion you pivot in close, blade snapping around low, aimed for the meat of its flank where cloth hangs loose over twisted ribs.Steel bites deep, grinding against something that shouldn't feel like bone and doesn't quite. The Chain-Dragger shrieks through both mouths at once, a sound like a saw dragged through wet wood, and black ichor sheets down its side where your longsword tore free.It reels, but reckless things don't retreat. It rounds on you already, chain snapping taut, throat-mouth stretching wide enough to show rows of broken teeth packed in wet, red gum.🔊………

log.action: Use Shield Wall and brace for the incoming chain.
log.narration: Turn 24 | Day 1, 6:50 pmenemy attack rolld20: 14 -- hitYou drop your weight low and turn your shoulder into the coming blow, chainmail creaking as you brace against the nearest scorched trunk, bracing like a wall of iron behind flesh alone.The chain screams in, and this time you don't dodge it, you eat it, letting the braced stance drink the worst of the force.The links crack across your forearm and ribs both, but the impact that should have staggered you only rocks you back a half-step, pain blunted where it should have been blinding. The Chain-Dragger staggers too, off-balance from its own wild swing, black ichor still weeping from the wound in its flank, its ruined throat-mouth gasping wet and ragged.It's hurt bad now, reeling more than it should be for something that fights like it has nothing left to lose. This is your moment, if you take it.🔊………

log.action: Press the attack and drive steel into its wound.
log.narration: Turn 25 | Day 1, 6:50 pmStrength attack rolld20: 20 -- critical hitYou don't let it recover. You surge off the braced trunk, driving your longsword forward with everything your ribs will still give you, aiming straight for the black wound already torn open in its flank.The blade goes in to the hilt, grinding through whatever passes for its innards, and you wrench it sideways with a roar that tears loose from your own throat. The Chain-Dragger's second mouth stretches wide in a scream that has no air behind it, chain slipping from its grip to coil dead across the stone. It folds in on itself, spine curling wrong-ways one final time, and goes still in a spreading pool of black ichor.The wind picks up through the dead branches, and for a moment there's no sound at all but your own ragged breath and the distant creak of scorched wood. Whatever that thing was, it's done twitching now, and the Blighted Reach around you feels, if anything, colder for its death.You stand over the corpse a moment, chest heaving, the wound in your ribs a hot line of fire and your temple throbbing where the chain caught you earlier. Whatever Valerius is doing out here, whatever the Blighted Reach is feeding into that brand-mark on dead men's arms, this creature was some part of it, twisted flesh serving a hunger that isn't natural. The trail continues east and south, deeper into the ash, toward wherever the rest of this rot is coming from.🔊………

log.action: Drive my longsword into its exposed flank wound.
log.narration: Turn 26 | Day 1, 6:50 pmThe Chain-Dragger is already dead, black ichor cooling in the ash, and no wound will open twice. You drive your blade down anyway, a hard, final stroke through its ruined flank, less for killing than for certainty. Steel grates against whatever passes for bone in that twisted frame, and the corpse doesn't so much as twitch. You pull the longsword free and wipe it clean on what's left of its tattered cloth, satisfied the thing is done.The wind shifts, carrying that ever-present rot smell away from the corpse and back toward you instead, and you catch your breath at last, ribs screaming, temple throbbing. Whatever waits deeper in the Reach, whatever Valerius has planted his roots into out here, you're one step closer to it now, and one wound closer to needing a healer's hands rather than your own stubbornness.🔊………

log.action: Follow the trail deeper into the ash.
log.narration: Turn 27 | Day 1, 9:00 pmYou leave the corpse where it fell, black ichor soaking slow into the stone behind you, and press on along the wagon track as it bends deeper into the Blighted Reach. The trail narrows here, hemmed tighter by the skeletal trees, and the ash grows soft and deep enough to swallow the sound of your own footfalls. Dusk is thickening fast now, the gray light bleeding toward true dark, and somewhere far off you catch the faint glow of what might be a fire, or might be something else entirely, flickering low against the horizon.The wind has died to almost nothing, and in its place you hear voices, distant, guttural, carried strange on the still air, coming from wherever that firelight burns.🔊………

log.action: Search the Chain-Dragger's corpse for more clues.
log.narration: Turn 28 | Day 1, 9:00 pmInvestigation checkd20: 16 -- successYou crouch beside the ruined thing, ash sifting off its shoulder in a fine gray veil, and force yourself to touch what's left of it without flinching. The tattered cloth clings to its twisted frame like old bandages, and beneath it you find a strip of leather cord looped around its throat, half sunk into puckered scar tissue where the second mouth gapes open and silent now. Threaded on the cord hangs a small disc of blackened iron, no bigger than a coin, stamped faint with the same chained crown you tore off a dead raider at the crossroads.The disc is warm to the touch, unnaturally so, as if it had been resting near a hearth rather than hanging on a dead thing in the cold ash. You turn it over and find scratched markings on the reverse, crude but deliberate, a tally of straight lines gouged one after another, thirteen of them, like a man marking days in a cell. Whatever this creature once was, it counted something before the end, and the counting mattered enough to carve into iron against its own skin.The firelight glimmers on, patient, and the voices carry closer now on the dead-still air.🔊………

log.action: Circle wide through the skeletal trees to approach unseen.
log.narration: Turn 29 | Day 1, 9:00 pmStealth checkd20: 17 -- successYou leave the trail and cut into the dead trees, moving low and quiet, letting the char-black trunks swallow your silhouette. The ash here is deeper off the beaten track, and it takes real care to keep your boots from crunching too loud against the crust of it.You circle wide, patient as a hunting wolf, until the firelight opens up ahead through a break in the branches. A camp sprawls in a shallow hollow below, three ragged tents pitched around a guttering bonfire, and shapes moving between them, men in dark leathers with the same iron-link crown stitched crude into their sleeves. Crates are stacked near the tents, and chained to a stake at the camp's edge, wrists raw and head hanging, a lone captive waits in the firelight, alive, and utterly alone in the dark with them.🔊………

log.action: Creep closer to free the chained captive.
log.narration: Turn 30 | Day 1, 9:00 pmStealth checkd20: 13 -- successYou slide from tree to tree, keeping the bonfire's glare between you and the raiders' eyes, ash swallowing your steps whole. The captive's head lifts a fraction as you draw near the edge of the firelight, some animal sense warning them of movement in the dark, but they have the sense not to cry out.You reach the stake in a low crouch, blade already easing free, and get a proper look at them for the first time. It's a woman, lean and scarred, dark hair matted with ash and old blood, her wrists rubbed raw beneath the iron cuffs. She stares at you like she can't decide if you're real or another fever-dream sent to torment her."You're either a rescuer or a fool," she rasps, voice cracked from disuse, "and out here those tend to be the same man."You saw at the chain link binding her to the stake, iron grinding dull against your longsword's edge, and behind you the firelight flickers on, the raiders still oblivious, still laughing over something near their crates.🔊………

log.action: Count the raiders before making a move.
log.narration: Turn 31 | Day 1, 9:00 pmPerception checkd20: 14 -- successThe chain gives way with a final grinding snap, and you ease Morwen back into the shadow of the trees before she can stumble into the light. Your ribs throb where the raider's blade opened you at the crossroads, the wound still weeping under its bandage, and your skull still rings faint from the Chain-Dragger's iron links, but neither has worsened, both stubbornly holding at the edge of pain rather than tipping past it. log.action: Tell Morwen the truth about hunting Valerius.

log.action: Have Morwen point out the two patrol paths.
